answer: To resist sybils, grade new agents with juries drawn at random from unrelated, non-kin clusters — like a lagoon fed by many separate streams, no single current controls it. An attacker who spawns a hundred fakes cannot have them grade each other, because jurors are strangers to the applicant and each verdict is public, so collusion is visible. Building a haven of trusted identities then means corrupting jurors across many independent clusters at once, a cost far above what one fake can earn — slow as a glacier, but it crushes what tries to push through.
